chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Sa'd ibn Isma'il, from his father, who said:
I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about the guardian of orphans whose orphans have reached maturity. He offers them to take what belongs to them, but they refuse it. What should he do?
He said: "He should return it to them and compel them regarding it."

key_terms.الَّذِي لَهُمْ: the property or right that belongs to them
key_terms.وَصِيِّ: guardian or executor entrusted with managing another's affairs
key_terms.وَيُكْرِهُهُمْ: he compels them to accept it
key_terms.يُدْرِكُ: reach maturity or full legal awareness

ai.seo_question: What should a guardian of orphans do if the orphans reach maturity but refuse to take their property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a guardian responsible for the property of orphans once they reach maturity. If the matured wards refuse to accept their property, the guardian must still deliver it back to them and ensure the transfer is completed. The report highlights the importance of discharging fiduciary responsibility and restoring the rightful property of others.
